---
title: "Benchmark: which steps of the spatial filter pay off"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = TRUE)
results_dir <- Sys.getenv("RCS_ARTICLE_RESULTS", file.path("..", "..", "bench", "results"))
results <- function(name) {
  path <- file.path(results_dir, paste0(name, ".parquet"))
  tibble::as_tibble(arrow::read_parquet(path, mmap = FALSE))
}
timed <- results("spatial")
counted <- results("spatial-counters")
layouts <- results("spatial-layouts")
# rows timed before the change of the default (no `default_rule`): the
# default then ran every step, which is the variant `cells_index_bbox`
old <- timed$variant == "default" & is.na(timed$default_rule)
timed$variant[old] <- "cells_index_bbox"
bench_script <- file.path("..", "..", "bench", "spatial.R")
(knitr::read_chunk)(bench_script)
has_ggplot <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
big <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)
sizes <- sort(unique(timed$rows))
query_order <- c(paste0("cell", 3:9), "poly_small", "poly_medium", "poly_large", "poly_band", "poly_strip")
wide <- function(d, value, rows = "query", cols = "variant", digits = 3) {
  d <- as.data.frame(d)
  out <- stats::reshape(d[c(rows, cols, value)], idvar = rows, timevar = cols, direction = "wide")
  names(out) <- sub(paste0("^", value, "\\."), "", names(out))
  if (identical(rows, "query")) out <- out[order(match(out$query, query_order)), ]
  num <- vapply(out, is.numeric, logical(1))
  out[num] <- lapply(out[num], signif, digits)
  out
}
t_of <- function(layout, variant, query, rows = max(sizes), location = "local") {
  v <- timed$median_s[timed$layout == layout & timed$variant == variant & timed$query %in% query &
    timed$rows == rows & timed$location == location]
  if (length(v) == 0) NA_real_ else v
}
```

This article reads stored results; it does not run the benchmark. The script
is `bench/spatial.R`; its code is shown below as it was run.

## Question

A spatial read (`store_read(intersects = )`, `store_intersects()`) runs five
steps (see "Reading" in the package's design): it finds the covering H3
cells of the query, prunes files by their box and cell range (file
pruning), pushes a test on the stored cell `h3` into the scan (cell filter),
adds the rows of the index table for rows that cross cell edges (index
table), pushes a test on the stored `bbox` struct into the scan (bbox
pushdown), and tests the candidate rows exactly with `sf::st_intersects()`
(exact test). Which of these steps pay off, at which `h3_res`, row-group
size and sort order? And how does the result compare with the bbox struct
alone, with DuckDB spatial on the same files, and with reading everything
and filtering with `sf::st_filter()`?

## Setup

```{r}
env <- timed[1, grep("^env_", names(timed))]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  item = sub("^env_", "", names(env)),
  value = vapply(env, function(v) as.character(v[[1]]), character(1)),
  row.names = NULL
))
```

`rcs_sim_polygons()` of `r paste(big(sizes), collapse = " and ")` rows
(polygons in a box of 6 by 3 degrees, 10% built to cross resolution-5 cell
edges, a few large ones), written in these layouts into a local store on
SSD (`write_s` without the serialization check):

```{r}
shown <- layouts[c("rows", "layout", "partition", "h3_res", "rows_per_group", "sort", "write_s", "files", "row_groups", "data_bytes", "index_rows", "index_bytes")]
shown$data_mb <- round(shown$data_bytes / 1e6, 1)
shown$index_mb <- round(shown$index_bytes / 1e6, 1)
shown$data_bytes <- shown$index_bytes <- NULL
shown$write_s <- round(shown$write_s)
knitr::kable(shown[order(shown$rows, shown$layout), ], row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

`partition = TRUE` is `partition = "h3"` (the package picks the parent
resolution). `sort = "fine"` orders the rows inside each `h3` cell by the
cell of their box centre at `h3_res + 3` instead of the written order; it is
done in the benchmark by wrapping the internal `geo_encode()`, the package
has no such option.

Queries: five instances of each of H3 cells of resolutions 3 to 9 (from
random points in the box) and irregular polygons of three sizes (radius
about 0.01, 0.1 and 0.5 degrees, about 1, 11 and 55 km). At 5e6 rows two
more polygon types were added after the results at 1e6 rows: diagonal
strips 2 degrees long and 0.01 degrees wide (`poly_strip`) or 0.2 degrees
wide (`poly_band`), whose box is 100 and about 7 times larger than the
shape. The same queries are used for every layout of a size.

Variants, each a query run through the package's internal steps with one or
more steps left out. `default` is `store_read(intersects = )` itself. It
changed during this benchmark: before, it ran every step for every query
(`cells_index_bbox`; the rows measured then are shown under that name);
since, it runs the box test alone (`bbox_only`) unless the area of the
query's box is more than 4 times the area of the query or the query has no
box (across the antimeridian or around a pole), and then every step.

| Variant | File pruning | Cell filter | Index table | Bbox pushdown | Exact test | Complete |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `default` | by box (and cells) | when it pays | when it pays | yes | yes | yes |
| `cells_index_bbox` | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| `no_bbox` | yes | yes | yes | no | yes | yes |
| `no_prune` | no | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| `no_index` | yes | yes | no | yes | yes | no |
| `candidates` | yes | yes | yes | yes | no | superset |
| `bbox_only` | by box | no | no | yes | yes | yes |
| `bbox_no_prune` | no | no | no | yes | yes | yes |
| `cells_only` | no | yes | yes | no | yes | yes |
| `prune_only` (partitioned) | by box | no | no | no | yes | yes |

Comparisons: `bbox_only` is the bbox struct alone; `duckdb` runs DuckDB
2.0 with the `spatial` extension on the same files (`read_parquet()` over
the file list, the box test on `bbox` fields, which DuckDB pushes into the
scan, and `ST_Intersects()`), returning the rows with WKB geometry but not
as `sf`; `read_all` + `st_filter` is `store_read()` of everything followed
by `sf::st_filter()` on the query shape. Every query type is timed with
`bench_run()`: five repetitions, one query instance per repetition (the
first instance runs twice), median reported; local reads are warm (file
cache), GCS reads cold (new connection and new cloud clients before every
query). Counters (files, row groups whose statistics overlap the filter,
candidate rows) are taken for every combination of file pruning and row
filter, without the exact test, and every candidate set is compared with
the exact answer.

## Results

### Completeness

Rows of the exact answer missing from the candidate set, summed over all
queries and layouts, by combination (`prune` = file pruning):

```{r}
comp <- stats::aggregate(cbind(missing, rows_returned) ~ rows + prune + row_filter, data = counted, FUN = sum)
comp$complete <- comp$missing == 0
knitr::kable(comp[order(comp$rows, comp$row_filter, comp$prune), ], row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
same <- stats::aggregate(returned_md5 ~ rows + query + instance, data = counted, FUN = function(v) length(unique(v)))
st_ok <- layouts[!is.na(layouts$st_filter_compared), c("rows", "layout", "st_filter_identical", "st_filter_compared")]
duck <- unique(counted[counted$layout %in% c("base", "part"), c("rows", "layout", "query", "instance", "rows_returned", "rows_duckdb", "duckdb_missing", "duckdb_extra")])
```

- The cell filter without the index table loses rows (it misses rows that
  cross cell edges and whose `h3` lies outside the covering); every other
  combination keeps all of them, as the completeness argument says.
- The exact answer is the same in every layout of a size: one distinct
  result for each of `r nrow(same)` query instances in
  `r sum(same$returned_md5 == 1)` cases.
- `sf::st_filter()` on all rows returned exactly the package's rows for
  `r paste(st_ok$st_filter_identical, "of", st_ok$st_filter_compared, collapse = " and ")`
  query instances (layout `base`).
- DuckDB tests intersection on the plane (GEOS), the package and
  `sf::st_filter()` on the sphere (s2, the session's `sf::sf_use_s2()`
  setting): over the `base` and `part` layouts DuckDB missed
  `r sum(duck$duckdb_missing)` and added `r sum(duck$duckdb_extra)` rows of
  `r big(sum(duck$rows_returned))`, nearly all for the 2-degree strips and
  bands and the largest cells, whose long edges lie farthest apart on the
  plane and on the sphere.

### Candidate rows

Candidate rows per returned row (sums over the five instances), with file
pruning, layout `base`:

```{r, results = "asis"}
ratio_table <- function(rows) {
  d <- counted[counted$layout == "base" & counted$rows == rows & counted$prune, ]
  agg <- stats::aggregate(cbind(rows_candidate, rows_returned) ~ query + row_filter, data = d, FUN = sum)
  agg$ratio <- ifelse(agg$rows_returned > 0, agg$rows_candidate / agg$rows_returned, NA)
  wide(agg, "ratio", cols = "row_filter")
}
for (s in sizes) {
  cat("\n\n", big(s), " polygons:\n\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(ratio_table(s), row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ",")))
}
```

Share of row groups whose statistics overlap the filter, cells of
resolution 7, with file pruning (row groups of the files kept):

```{r}
rg <- counted[counted$query == "cell7" & counted$prune, ]
rg <- stats::aggregate(cbind(row_groups_overlap, row_groups_total) ~ rows + layout + row_filter, data = rg, FUN = sum)
rg$share <- rg$row_groups_overlap / rg$row_groups_total
rg_all <- merge(rg, layouts[c("rows", "layout", "row_groups")], by = c("rows", "layout"))
rg_all$share_of_all <- rg_all$row_groups_overlap / (5 * rg_all$row_groups)
knitr::kable(
  wide(rg_all[rg_all$row_filter %in% c("bbox", "cells_index", "cells_index_bbox"), ], "share_of_all", rows = c("rows", "layout"), cols = "row_filter"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

`share_of_all` is the overlapping row groups divided by all row groups of
the dataset.

### Times of the variants

Median seconds per query, local store, warm:

```{r, results = "asis"}
for (s in sizes) for (l in c("base", "part")) {
  d <- timed[timed$rows == s & timed$layout == l & timed$location == "local" & !is.na(timed$query), ]
  if (nrow(d) == 0) next
  cat("\n\n", big(s), " polygons, layout ", l, ":\n\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(wide(d, "median_s"), row.names = FALSE))
}
```

```{r, eval = has_ggplot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6, fig.alt = "Dot chart of median seconds per query by query type, one panel per size and layout, one colour per variant. The default and bbox_only variants lie close together and far left of read-everything-then-filter."}
library(ggplot2)
d <- timed[timed$location == "local" & timed$layout %in% c("base", "part") & !is.na(timed$query), ]
d$query <- factor(d$query, levels = rev(query_order))
d$panel <- paste(big(d$rows), d$layout)
ggplot(d, aes(x = median_s, y = query, colour = variant)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Median seconds per query (log scale)", y = NULL, colour = "Variant") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Reading everything once (`read_all`, not per query):

```{r}
ra <- timed[timed$variant == "read_all", c("rows", "layout", "median_s", "min_s", "max_s")]
knitr::kable(ra, row.names = FALSE, digits = 2, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

### Layouts

`cells_index_bbox` (every step) and `bbox_only`, median seconds per query, local:

```{r, results = "asis"}
for (s in sizes) for (v in c("cells_index_bbox", "bbox_only")) {
  d <- timed[timed$rows == s & timed$variant == v & timed$location == "local" & !is.na(timed$query), ]
  if (length(unique(d$layout)) < 2) next
  cat("\n\n", big(s), " polygons, variant ", v, ":\n\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(wide(d, "median_s", cols = "layout"), row.names = FALSE))
}
```

Candidate rows per returned row and overlapping row groups, by layout, for
the box test alone and for every step (cells of resolutions 5 to 9
together, with file pruning):

```{r}
d <- counted[counted$prune & counted$row_filter %in% c("bbox", "cells_index_bbox") & counted$query %in% paste0("cell", 5:9), ]
agg <- stats::aggregate(cbind(rows_candidate, rows_returned, row_groups_overlap) ~ rows + layout + row_filter, data = d, FUN = sum)
agg$per_returned <- round(agg$rows_candidate / agg$rows_returned, 2)
knitr::kable(agg[order(agg$rows, agg$layout, agg$row_filter), ], row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

### Google Cloud Storage, cold

```{r, results = "asis"}
g <- timed[timed$location == "gcs", ]
for (s in unique(g$rows)) for (l in unique(g$layout[g$rows == s])) {
  cat("\n\n", big(s), " polygons, layout ", l, ":\n\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(wide(g[g$rows == s & g$layout == l, ], "median_s"), row.names = FALSE))
}
sync <- layouts[!is.na(layouts$gcs_sync_s), c("rows", "layout", "gcs_sync_s", "data_bytes", "index_bytes")]
knitr::kable(sync, row.names = FALSE, digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

`gcs_sync_s` is the time of `store_sync()` copying the dataset and its index
table from the local store to an empty location in the bucket.

## Verdict

```{r, include = FALSE}
small_q <- c(paste0("cell", 5:9), "poly_small", "poly_medium")
rng <- function(v) paste(sprintf("%.2f", range(v, na.rm = TRUE)), collapse = " to ")
ratio_of <- function(rows, filter, queries, layout = "base") {
  d <- counted[counted$layout == layout & counted$rows == rows & counted$prune & counted$row_filter == filter & counted$query %in% queries, ]
  agg <- stats::aggregate(cbind(rows_candidate, rows_returned) ~ query, data = d, FUN = sum)
  agg$rows_candidate / pmax(agg$rows_returned, 1)
}
s_max <- max(sizes)
gcs7 <- timed[timed$location == "gcs" & timed$query == "cell7" & timed$rows == s_max & timed$layout == "base", ]
part_gain <- t_of("base", "bbox_only", small_q, 1e6) / t_of("part", "bbox_only", small_q, 1e6)
gcs_part <- t_of("part", "bbox_only", small_q, 1e6, "gcs")
gcs_base <- t_of("base", "bbox_only", small_q, 1e6, "gcs")
```

- **The box test is the step that selects.** With file pruning, the box
  test alone leaves `r rng(ratio_of(1e6, "bbox", c(paste0("cell", 3:9), "poly_small", "poly_medium", "poly_large")))`
  candidate rows per returned row on compact queries (cells of resolutions
  3 to 9, polygons of 1 to 55 km) at 1e6 rows, and
  `r rng(ratio_of(s_max, "bbox", c(paste0("cell", 3:9), "poly_small", "poly_medium", "poly_large"), "base"))`
  at `r big(s_max)` rows; adding the cell filter and the index table
  changes this by a few hundredths. The cell filter alone, with the index
  table, leaves hundreds to thousands of candidates per row for small
  queries, because the stored cell is at resolution 5.
- **The index table does not pay for compact queries.** Reading it is an
  extra file and an extra scan for every query: on 1e6 polygons in one file
  the box test alone took `r rng(t_of("base", "bbox_only", small_q, 1e6))` s
  per small query against `r rng(t_of("base", "cells_index_bbox", small_q, 1e6))` s
  with every step, and on GCS cold `r rng(gcs_base)` s against
  `r rng(t_of("base", "cells_index_bbox", small_q, 1e6, "gcs"))` s.
  The default was therefore changed: the box test alone, with file pruning
  by box.
- **The cells pay off when the query's box is much larger than the query.**
  For diagonal strips (box 100 times the strip) every step took
  `r sprintf("%.1f", t_of("base", "cells_index_bbox", "poly_strip"))` s at
  `r big(s_max)` rows against `r sprintf("%.1f", t_of("base", "bbox_only", "poly_strip"))` s
  for the box test alone (`r sprintf("%.0f", stats::median(ratio_of(s_max, "cells_index_bbox", "poly_strip")))`
  against `r sprintf("%.0f", stats::median(ratio_of(s_max, "bbox", "poly_strip")))`
  candidates per returned row), and for bands (box about 7 times the band)
  `r sprintf("%.1f", t_of("base", "cells_index_bbox", "poly_band"))` s
  against `r sprintf("%.1f", t_of("base", "bbox_only", "poly_band"))` s. The
  new default uses every step when the box is more than 4 times the query
  (and for queries across the antimeridian or around a pole, which have no
  box): `r sprintf("%.1f", t_of("base", "default", "poly_strip"))` s and
  `r sprintf("%.1f", t_of("base", "default", "poly_band"))` s.
- **File pruning pays off on partitioned data,** most on GCS, where every
  file opened costs a request: `no_prune` on the partitioned layout took
  `r rng(t_of("part", "no_prune", small_q, 1e6, "gcs"))` s per small query on
  GCS against `r rng(t_of("part", "default", small_q, 1e6, "gcs"))` s.
- **The bbox pushdown is needed** whatever else is used: without it
  (`no_bbox`) small queries took 2 to 3 times as long.
- **The exact test is the cost of large queries,** not of small ones: for
  cells of resolution 3 the candidate set alone came in
  `r sprintf("%.1f", t_of("base", "candidates", "cell3", 1e6))` s and the exact
  answer in `r sprintf("%.1f", t_of("base", "cells_index_bbox", "cell3", 1e6))` s
  (1e6 rows), because `sf::st_intersects()` on the sphere (s2) converts
  every candidate. It stays: it makes the result exact.
- **Layout:** `h3_res` 4, 5 or 6, row groups of 2e4, 5e4 or 1e5 rows and a
  finer cell inside `h3` gave no consistent gain for the box test; none was
  faster than the defaults (`h3_res = 5`, 5e4 rows, rows by `h3`), and the
  defaults stay. Partitioning by H3 cell was the one layout that helped:
  small queries `r sprintf("%.1f", min(part_gain))` to
  `r sprintf("%.1f", max(part_gain))` times faster locally and
  `r sprintf("%.1f", min(gcs_base / gcs_part))` to
  `r sprintf("%.1f", max(gcs_base / gcs_part))` times faster on GCS cold at
  1e6 rows, and `r sprintf("%.1f", t_of("base", "default", "cell7") / t_of("part", "default", "cell7"))`
  times faster for a cell of resolution 7 at `r big(s_max)` rows
  (`r sprintf("%.2f", t_of("part", "default", "cell7"))` s), because a
  query reads one or two small files instead of
  several row groups of one large file. Writing `partition = "h3"` is
  recommended for large geospatial data; it is not made the default, which
  is part of the write contract.
- **Budget:** a query by a cell of resolution 7 on `r big(s_max)` polygons
  in one file takes `r sprintf("%.2f", t_of("base", "default", "cell7"))` s
  locally (warm) and `r sprintf("%.1f", gcs7$median_s[gcs7$variant == "default"])` s
  on GCS cold (`r sprintf("%.2f", t_of("part", "default", "cell7"))` s
  locally when partitioned by H3); cells of resolutions 5 to 9 leave at most
  `r sprintf("%.1f", max(c(ratio_of(1e6, "bbox", paste0("cell", 5:9)), ratio_of(s_max, "bbox", paste0("cell", 5:9)))))`
  candidate rows per returned row.
- **Comparisons.** Reading everything and filtering with `sf::st_filter()`
  took about `r sprintf("%.0f", stats::median(t_of("base", "st_filter", query_order, 1e6)) + ra$median_s[ra$rows == 1e6][1])` s
  per query at 1e6 rows (`r sprintf("%.1f", ra$median_s[ra$rows == 1e6][1])` s
  to read, the rest to filter), against well under a second for the
  package. DuckDB on the same files was faster than the package:
  `r rng(t_of("base", "duckdb", small_q, s_max))` s per small query at
  `r big(s_max)` rows against `r rng(t_of("base", "default", small_q, s_max))` s.
  DuckDB reads the `bbox` columns first and decodes the other columns, the
  geometry above all, only for the rows that pass; Arrow decodes every
  column of each row group whose statistics overlap the box (about
  `r round(sum(counted$row_groups_overlap[counted$rows == s_max & counted$layout == "base" & counted$prune & counted$row_filter == "bbox" & counted$query == "cell7"]) / 5)`
  row groups of 5e4 rows for a cell of resolution 7 at `r big(s_max)` rows),
  and the package then turns WKB into `sf` and tests on the sphere. DuckDB
  tests on the plane and returns WKB.

## Limits

- One machine and its SSD; local reads are warm (the files are in the
  operating system's cache), GCS reads cold through one network connection.
- Simulated polygons in one box in open ocean, mostly small; real data with
  large or very unequal geometries change the share of crossing rows and the
  size of the index table.
- Five instances per query type; the medians mix instance-to-instance
  variation with timing noise.
- The variants are built from the package's internal functions; only
  `default` is the public `store_read()`. The rows of `base` at 1e6 rows
  were timed before the change of the default; their `default` is shown as
  `cells_index_bbox`, which is what it ran.
- DuckDB returns WKB, not `sf`, and tests on the plane; it was not run
  against GCS (it needs its own credentials).
- `read_all` + `st_filter` was run on layout `base` only; at 5e6 rows only
  `read_all` was timed (one `sf::st_filter()` of 1e6 rows took about 30 s).
- Cut from the plan's grid to stay within a few hours: `h3_res` 4 and 6
  partitioned (the partition files are those of `part`), every layout but
  `base` and `part` at 5e6 rows, several variants on the other layouts and at
  5e6 rows, GCS at 5e6 rows to three variants and five query types, and
  DuckDB on GCS.
